description: Fermi estimate of a public CBAM calculation tool: Expected-value estimate for building a public, source-bound CBAM (Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism) calculation tool, conditional on the stated premise that a usable tool causes an additional 10% reduction in global GHG emissions within one year. The calculation is the "expected value of a tool build" formula, whose inputs are the values of this file. Reported outcome: P(usable) 0.028, value of the 10 percent reduction 1'096'300'000'000 USD per year (range 692'400'000'000 to 1'961'800'000'000), expected value 29'200'000'000 USD. One-year, non-compounding effect only, per the stated premise. If the effect is assumed durable/annual, NPV over 10y at 5% discount scales roughly x7.7. Sensitivity: the cost-effectiveness case (build_cost vs. EV) is positive even at P(usable) as low as 0.0001 (EV ~110M USD, still >>build_cost). The result is therefore almost entirely determined by the 10 percent causal premise, not by cost or adoption probability.

triples.name: public CBAM calculation tool
triples.description: Publicly usable, source-verifiable tool for calculating carbon-border-adjustment obligations, in the zukunft.com sense of numbers bound to word/triple/source chains

triples.name: greenhouse gas emission
triples.description: Release of a greenhouse gas into the atmosphere.

triples.name: global greenhouse gas emissions
triples.description: Total global greenhouse gas emissions, all sectors including LULUCF

triples.name: social cost of carbon
triples.description: EPA 2023 central estimate, 2020 USD per metric ton CO2, 2% near-term discount rate

triples.name: causal chain
triples.description: The assumed mechanism: public tool -> supply-chain transparency -> closes carbon-leakage gap -> changes importer behavior -> tightens policy -> global emissions effect. Stated as a premise by the user, NOT independently derived or verified here.

triples.name: build cost
triples.description: one-off cost of building the tool

triples.name: technical completion
triples.description: the tool is finished and technically functional

triples.name: effect-relevant adoption
triples.description: the finished tool is adopted widely enough to drive the assumed emissions effect
US dollars per metric tonne of CO2, in 2020 USD at a 2 percent near-term discount rate

triples.name: confidence value
triples.description: The p-value of an assumed value: the subjective probability between 0 and 1 that the tagged estimate is right.

triples.name: usable probability
triples.description: The probability that the tool ends up usable, which is the product of the technical completion and the effect-relevant adoption probability.

formulas.name: usable probability of a tool
formulas.description: A tool is usable only if it is both technically finished and adopted widely enough to matter, so the two probabilities multiply.

formulas.name: expected value of a tool build
formulas.expression: "expected value" = "usable probability" * "greenhouse gas emission reduction" * "global greenhouse gas emissions" * "social cost of carbon" - "build cost"
formulas.description: The avoided damage that the tool is expected to cause, valued with the social cost of carbon, minus what building it costs.
